title.official: Actions by and against sole proprietors

operative_text.controlling:
2.5(1)  If a person carries on business or operates as a sole
proprietor under a name other than the person’s name, the person
may bring or be the subject of an action in that name.
(2)  If an action is brought by or against a person in the person’s
business or operating name, a party may serve a notice requiring
the person to disclose, in writing, the legal name of the person
carrying on the business or operation.
(3)  The person on whom the notice to disclose is served must
comply with it within 10 days after the date the notice is served.

BOOK_A.title: Actions By and Against Sole Proprietors
BOOK_A.related_provisions: 5.28 (written questions) ; 5.5 (discovery of records) ; 6.37 (notice to admit) ; 11.12 and 11.13 (service where trade name used)
BOOK_A.commentary:
Rule 2.5 may not apply to other unincorporated bodies, such as clubs or associations. Rule
2.5 now extends the beneﬁts of R.2.2 to an individual defendant who carried on business under
a different name, e. g. , Joe Smith carrying on business as Joe’s Auto Body. It now extends to a
plaintiff doing that.²

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.83. It came from 1944 C. R.97(i).

Quite similar to previous 1968 R.80(3) -(5). It came from pt.1944 C. R.97; Common Law Procedure Act 1852 s.7; 1883 O.7 r.2; O.48A. R.1; 1914 R.146(c) (second half) ; 914 R.146(a), and 1944 C. R.97(a).
footnotes.review_flag: attached to 2.5(3); same history note as rule 2.4 (1968 R.80(3)-(5)). 2.5(2)-(3) have a similar notice to disclose (not identical - no equivalent of 2.4(3)-(4)); whether 1968 R.80(3)-(5) is really their source cannot be checked from the sources (6th pass removed an earlier 'plausible' judgment). Source typo: '914 R.146(a)' should read '1914 R.146(a)'. 2.5(1)'s own history is footnote 3 on page 2-5 (1968 R.83).

footnotes.text: Compare the previous rule and the C. P. E. , Chapter 69, esp. Part N. Previously, if a sole proprietor sued in her trade name, whether or not she had a right to use that name, and whether or not it sounded like a company name, that was a (curable) irregularity: RC Int. v. Brooks (Gatenby) (#1) 2000 ABCA 204, 261 AR 329.

BOOK_C.title: Actions by and against sole proprietors

commentary.text: It is permissible pursuant to this rule for a person to sue or be sued in the name of an unincorporated business. As the business is not incorporated it has no legal personality. Normal practice would see the proprietor being sued in their own name along with the name of the unregistered business. One can sue, for example, a “John Doe carrying on business as Corner Pizza”. The legal entity is the natural or artificial person behind the firm or tradename. Stamos v. Huculuk, [2018] A.J. No. 925, 2018 ABQB 566 at para. 3 (Alta. Q.B.).

under trade names are contained in rule 11.12 [Service on individuals using another name]
and rule 11.13 [Service on a corporation using another name].

Rule 2.2: BOOK_A's 2.5 commentary says 2.5 'extends the benefits of R.2.2' (suing in a firm name) to an individual trading under another name, plaintiff or defendant.

Rule 2.4: a similar 'notice to disclose' (comply within 10 days); 2.4 alone adds a dispute/application step (2.4(3)) and last-known-address duty (2.4(4)); BOOK_A repeats 2.4's history note under 2.5(3).
Rule 2.6: BOOK_A says 2.5 'may not apply to ... clubs or associations'; BOOK_A's 2.6 commentary treats unincorporated associations (unions, yacht clubs) as suited to representative actions.
